# Preview renderer contract
All files here are isolated preview. Never edit parent dist files.
Each world exports createXWorld(container), returns { update(state, dt), destroy() }. Controller calls update every RAF with current engine state. Renderer draws actual meshes; may use scoped DOM labels in container. No keyboard/storage/listeners except resize owned renderer. Parent handles pause.
Engine state fields: level (1..12), mode ('catch','stone','forest','room','card','mail'), phase ('ready','playing','acting','complete'), paused boolean, step integer, accepted array of actual accepted keys, completed array (task/object IDs), selected string|null, held string|null, placements object keyed item label -> destination key, buffer string, route string|null, action {type,key,from,to,duration,elapsed}|null, wrongKey string|null, wrongUntil number, tasks array, choices array of {key,label,kind,position?,done?}, target string|null, message string, progress number, total number. State is JSON safe. Engine owns animation elapsed; render never mutates state. During acting choices refer prior/current action; completed/placements commit after animation. Renderer can read level and engine exports for specs. Engine worker will finalize details promptly; notify deviations.
World filenames: orchard-world.js (catch), river-world.js (stone), forest-world.js, pairing-world.js (room), invitation-world.js (card/mail). Imports existing assets via ../vendor or ../world.js etc; copy adapted modules into preview when needing edits. Main controller and map by owner. Scene-primary labels near objects, no giant central/bottom duplicate prompt. Ensure paused renders stable. Shared world can use HTML labels but real bear/object motion mandatory.

## Bounded lesson stages

Each level has `lessonStageIndex` 0–2. `stageReady` with `phase: 'stage-ready'` is a saved, input-blocked checkpoint, not level completion. The controller calls `advanceStage` explicitly. `stageHistory`, `stageStartAccepted`, and cumulative `accepted` retain real input counts; local `progress`/`total` refer only to the current stage. Renderers derive tasks from current arrays and reset on stage index changes. `initialPlacements`, `forkIndex`, and `picnicGuests` preserve room, multi-clue forest, and persistent picnic continuity. Save format2 reads legacy format1; `legacyCompleted` preserves existing completion, while `migrationNotice` explains resumed first-stage work.
